findings.title: Unchecked property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` sets `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array `[]` (which many callers now pass when no destination calendar is configured). Line 119 then evaluates `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever an event with Google Meet location is created for a user without a destination calendar.

findings.title: Unrelated inversion of `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` check when setting organization slug
findings.body: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, line 151 was changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously, when team billing was enabled, the slug was stored only in `metadata.requestedSlug` (until billing/payment completed) and not set directly on the organization; when team billing was disabled (e.g., self-hosted), the slug was set immediately. This change inverts that logic and appears to be an unintended edit unrelated to `destinationCalendar`.

findings.title: Collective host destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
findings.body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set (lines 1063-1067). Immediately afterwards on line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on `null`, so if the primary organizer has no `destinationCalendar` configured, `teamDestinationCalendars` for all other collective hosts are silently discarded and their calendar events are never created. `evt.destinationCalendar` should be initialized to `[]` (or assigned `teamDestinationCalendars`) so other hosts' destination calendars are preserved.

findings.title: `calendar.events.patch` receives `undefined` `calendarId` instead of falling back to `"primary"`
findings.body: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which can be `undefined` (whereas previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 was updated to use `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call on line 168 (used to attach the Hangout/Meet link to the description) still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When `selectedCalendar` is `undefined`, the patch request will fail with a missing `calendarId`.

findings.title: Fallback lookup for `selectedCalendar` in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` is dead code
findings.body: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch when `externalCalendarId` is falsy searches `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Because this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`), comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` will never match a valid calendar's `externalId`, so the fallback always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, this leaves `selectedCalendar` as `undefined`, causing `calendar.events.update` to fail when `externalCalendarId` is not stored on the booking reference.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use `destinationCalendar[0]` instead of matching the current host's credential
findings.body: In `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` (line 128), `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (CalDAV, line 156), the target calendar is chosen via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` rather than finding the entry in `event.destinationCalendar` matching the `credentialId` being used (as `GoogleCalendarService` does). In a collective event where a non-main host uses Lark, Office365, or CalDAV, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` invokes `createEvent` with that host's credential, but the service will attempt to create the event in `destinationCalendar[0]?.externalId` (which belongs to the primary host and possibly a completely different provider), causing event creation to fail with a 404/invalid calendar ID.

findings.title: `updateEvent` called with `undefined` credential when DB lookup fails or app has no slug
findings.body: In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 515-542), if `reference.credentialId` is not in `this.calendarCredentials`, it queries `prisma.credential.findUnique`. If the credential was deleted or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy, `credential` remains `undefined`, yet line 542 unconditionally calls `updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId)`. Inside `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, accessing `credential.appName` / `credential.type` will throw a TypeError and abort all other calendar updates in the `try` block. Line 542 should guard with `if (credential)` just as `createAllCalendarEvents` does on line 369.
